reviews.text:
Thank you for your continued support. The clinic is conveniently located near the station, and the doctor listens attentively to my concerns. It's a trustworthy clinic.

I look forward to continuing to use your services.

Sub-chan, who has been suffering from a serious illness, is receiving care here.
Thanks to your help, he is recovering well!
Thank you.

I used their pet hotel service. I was happy that the entrances for cats and dogs were separate. The staff were very kind, and the head veterinarian was also very helpful and gave me lots of advice. Best of all, the price was very reasonable. Since it's a hospital, I felt safe leaving my pet there, and the reasonable price was a great help.

Many people park illegally on the street while they go to the doctor.
Or, one person goes to the doctor while the other waits in the car.
On bad days, there are 2 or 3 cars parked there, blocking the sidewalk and causing a nuisance.
I use their services every month. I feel completely at ease entrusting my dog's grooming to them, and they always do a great job!

We are grateful for the care we receive for our hospitalized cat. It was our first time having our cat hospitalized, and we were filled with anxiety, but the doctor and staff have been incredibly kind and attentive every time, allowing us to entrust our cat to their care with complete peace of mind.

During visits, they clearly explain the current condition and progress of the treatment, which has been a great relief as it allows us to resolve any small questions or concerns on the spot. Their gentle and loving approach to our cat is evident.

The clinic is always kept impeccably clean, providing a hygienic environment where we can leave our cat with complete confidence. We are so glad we entrusted our beloved family member to this clinic. We look forward to continuing to receive your care in the future.

Aries Animal Hospital is located about a 1-minute walk from Sasazuka Station.

The emerald green sign makes it easy to find.

It's conveniently located near the station, and the clinic is very clean and well-maintained.

My elderly cat is a patient there, and I'm always grateful for the kind and gentle care of the staff.

As my elderly cat gets older, her health changes more often, which can be worrying, but they always examine her carefully, and the atmosphere makes it easy to discuss even small concerns, which puts me at ease.

The fees are reasonable, and I appreciate that they work with me to consider a treatment plan that is manageable for my needs.

I think it's a wonderful hospital that not only cares for the animals but also understands the feelings of their owners.

I want to continue entrusting my beloved family member to this hospital with confidence.

Thank you always.

My rescue cat suddenly started staggering, so I took videos and photos before visiting the clinic.
I initially made an appointment, but I couldn't catch the cat and had to cancel that day. They were very kind and polite, saying I should bring her back once I caught her.

During the actual examination, the head veterinarian considered various possibilities, including injections, IV fluids, X-rays, and blood tests, to determine a treatment plan.

After the initial consultation at the beginning of March, including dietary therapy, the cat returned to a healthy state in about 1.5 months.

She is slightly overweight (fatty liver), so under the head veterinarian's guidance, I plan to visit again in about six months for a check-up.

My 12-year-old rabbit was nearly put at risk of death due to a misdiagnosis and the suggestion of unnecessary surgery. I took him in because his testicular area was swollen, but the vet just repeatedly touched it, saying they didn't know what it was, but suspected it was a tumor and surgery was the only option. The vet was also clumsy, holding the rabbit with one hand while standing. It was dangerous; he almost fell. Did they understand the risk of fracture?

Knowing that anesthesia can be fatal for elderly rabbits, I asked if surgery was truly the only option and what the risks of anesthesia were. They insisted the risks of not removing it were higher, and that it was likely malignant.

Suspicious, I took him for a second opinion, where the vet diagnosed it as an inguinal hernia, not a tumor, after just one look. Furthermore, they explained that most rabbit testicular tumors are benign, and considering the risks of anesthesia at his age, removal was rarely necessary.

My rabbit could have easily lost his life due to unnecessary surgery.

If you're going to advertise that you'll have exotic animals, you should study more first. Learn how to handle rabbits properly. You lack the necessary knowledge and experience.
